comparison: Both evaluate performance comparison claims (C18, C32-C33, C39-C51). OpenEval finds quantitative metrics and statistical validation sufficient. Peer reviewers raise significant concerns that CellPose and StarDist perform surprisingly poorly (often worse than Otsu thresholding), suggesting suboptimal training and questioning whether comparisons represent fair assessment of baseline capabilities.

Both address active learning results (C54, C86). OpenEval notes statistical validation with modest sample size. Peer reviewers acknowledge comprehensive evaluation including active learning without challenging these specific results.

Both evaluate zero-shot generalization claims (C56-C60, with peer also considering C19). OpenEval finds rigorous testing on external datasets supports broad applicability. Peer reviewers acknowledge testing on multiple datasets but question validity of comparisons due to concerns about baseline method training, noting WNet results are often only on par with Otsu thresholding.

Both address dataset creation claims. OpenEval evaluates novelty and methodology (C10-C12, C22, C69, C71-C73). Peer review focuses on dataset quality and annotation (C12, C22-C23, C69, C71-C73). Both find dataset contribution well-documented and validated through comprehensive evaluation.

Both address limitations of self-supervised approach (C52-C53). OpenEval finds honest acknowledgment of fundamental limitations. Peer reviewers raise concerns about post-processing and artifact removal impact on comparisons, questioning whether Otsu baseline received same treatment and whether artifact handling substantially affects reported accuracy.

Both evaluate training methodology (C82-C85). OpenEval finds procedures sufficiently detailed for reproduction and justifies retraining decisions. Peer reviewers directly challenge training optimality, suggesting CellPose and StarDist were not trained optimally given their poor performance relative to community expertise.

Both address model development claims (C17, C36-C38). OpenEval evaluates architectural specifications and modifications. Peer review (also including C66-C68, C70) acknowledges the self-supervised method and Napari plugin without challenging development claims.

Both evaluate software package and accessibility (C66-C68, C70). OpenEval documents availability through multiple platforms. Peer reviewers acknowledge the work is 'conveniently packaged as a Napari plugin' and note comprehensive evaluation without challenging accessibility claims.

Both address practical application example (C61). OpenEval notes qualitative demonstration of utility. Peer reviewers support practical relevance, with editor noting work will be 'of interest to a wide variety of laboratories' without challenging the application.

OpenEval evaluates baseline method descriptions (C24-C27, C29-C31) and finds them accurate with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific characterization claims.

OpenEval evaluates statistical methodology claims (C87-C88, C93-C94) and finds use of standard metrics and appropriate non-parametric tests. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific statistical method claims.
OpenEval evaluates background and motivation claims (C1-C9) and finds them supported by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature review claims.

OpenEval evaluates characterization of prior work on self-supervised methods (C13-C16, C34-C35) and finds accurate representation with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates acknowledgment of current limitations and future work (C62-C63) and finds honest representation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates scope limitation acknowledgment (C65) and finds appropriate scoping with citation of alternative tools. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates claims about current trends and applications (C20-C21) and finds them supported by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
